sources.title: New model reveals how water moves through tile-drained farm fields

en.title: NASA opens digital avatar challenge; Illinois study maps water movement in tile-drained fields
en.dek: NASA competition seeks digital twins of astronaut bone marrow chips; Illinois study uses 3D modeling to track farm-field water flow
facts: NASA's BPS Digital AVATAR Challenge invites the scientific community to apply computational digital twin technologies to model how the AVATAR bone marrow chip responds to spaceflight stressors.,The original AVATAR investigation flew aboard the Artemis II mission and returned organ-on-a-chip devices from crew cells after a 10-day lunar flyby.

University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign published a study in the Journal of Hydrology on high-resolution three-dimensional modeling of surface and subsurface water movement in tile-drained fields.,The study tested two approaches for representing tile drainage in the Advanced Terrestrial Simulator, finding that 2-meter resolution preserved local ponding patterns while 40-meter resolution smoothed out fine-scale features.
body: NASA has opened the BPS Digital AVATAR Challenge, inviting the scientific community to apply innovative computational digital twin technologies to accelerate biological discovery and predict individual astronaut health outcomes. The digital twin will be a computational model of how the AVATAR bone marrow chip responds to spaceflight stressors, building on the original AVATAR investigation that flew aboard the Artemis II mission and returned organ-on-a-chip devices from crew cells after a 10-day lunar flyby.

A new study from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, published in the Journal of Hydrology, addresses gaps in modeling water movement through tile-drained agricultural fields. Working with collaborators at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Illinois team used two tile-drained fields at the University of Illinois Energy Farm to evaluate how model resolution, microtopography, soil properties, and tile depth and spacing affected drainage.
en.context: NASA develops personalized health strategies for deep space crew members while agricultural researchers model water movement in farm fields to support crop growth and water quality.
